newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani cotton rates close steady, seen stable.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani cotton rates close steady, seen stable.

text.p: Pakistani cotton rates closed steady on Saturday as supplies from the new 1997/98 (July-June) crop matched the demand for it, dealers at the private Karachi Cotton Association (KCA) said.
Prices remained unchanged also because there was not much buying interest when the market reopened after Friday's religious holiday, one dealer said.
In the kerb market, the NIAB-78 variety was quoted at 2,340/2,360 rupees per maund (37.32 kg), the K-68 at 2,550/2,570 and the MNH-93 at 2,550/2,565.

The KCA said exporters had shipped 125,515 (375-lb) bales of cotton by June 28 compared to 1.82 million bales in the same time a year ago. Exporters had registered contracts for the export of 164,756 bales by July 8 compared to 2.32 million bales in the same time a year ago.
